title: Ceva's Theorem: Spherical Ceva via Unit Vectors and Weight Balance

problemStatement.formal: \\text{For unit vectors } A, B, C \\in V \\text{ with } \\|A\\|=\\|B\\|=\\|C\\|=1, \\text{ and cevian points } D = \\mathrm{normalize}(\\alpha_D B + \\beta_D C), E = \\mathrm{normalize}(\\alpha_E C + \\beta_E A), F = \\mathrm{normalize}(\\alpha_F A + \\beta_F B), \\text{ the spherical Ceva condition holds iff } \\alpha_D \\alpha_E \\alpha_F = \\beta_D \\beta_E \\beta_F.
problemStatement.plain: The spherical Ceva theorem expressed via weight parameters: cevian points on great circle arcs defined by normalizing weighted sums of unit vectors. The concurrency condition (product of sin-ratios = 1) is equivalent to the weight balance α_D·α_E·α_F = β_D·β_E·β_F.
whyMatters: Bridges abstract arc-length formulation with concrete algebraic criterion
Works in any real inner product space (all dimensions)
Computational: weight balance is simpler to check than sin-product

currentState.focus: Proof complete: 0 sorries, gallery entry created

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: CevasTheoremOQ02OQ01.lean (0 sorries). sin_ratio_cevian_point, spherical_ceva_product_eq_weight_ratio, spherical_ceva_iff_weight_balance all proved.
insights: sin(BD)/sin(DC) = β/α depends only on weight parameters, not geometry (√(1-m²)/n cancels)
Weight balance α_D·α_E·α_F = β_D·β_E·β_F is a purely algebraic concurrency criterion
Works in any dimension (any real inner product space, not just S²)
Key identity: n² - (α+βm)² = β²(1-m²) where n=‖αB+βC‖, m=⟪B,C⟫
